identity: Utrecht University BA English Language and Culture, full-time, primarily English, September 2026 entrants

sources.scope: Official prospective curriculum, programme identity and disciplinary interests.
Thesis preparation, independent supervision and two-assessor procedure.
2026–27 BA Thesis (EN3V14001) admission, supervised individual work and assessment.

curriculum: The 2026 entrant full-time BA is primarily taught in English with some Dutch under Clause 3.3. The 120 EC major comprises two 30 EC first-year core profiles, one 30 EC advanced specialisation, its 7.5 EC context course, one 7.5 EC methodology choice, the 7.5 EC Thesis Lab and the 7.5 EC BA thesis. Appendix 1 also requires the 0 EC Basic Grammar Test. Appendix 2 specifies Old English and Early Medieval Society, Language and Identity, Sociolinguistics of Englishes and World Englishes for The Social Life of English. The programme-specific EER controls the new entrant example, rather than substituting Historical Sociolinguistics from transitional material. Topics in Linguistics is required for this specialisation. Methods and Statistics 1 is the first of the four methodology choices. The four advanced specialisation courses, two advanced first-year courses and advanced thesis components provide 60 EC at level 3 and meet the 45 EC major minimum. The general BA is the exact target. The Celtic specialisation is listed with course codes pending and advertised as starting in 2027–28, so it is a prospective direction, not assumed to be running in 2026–27.
progression: The optional profile is 60 EC, including a 30 EC package such as a minor, study abroad or a second specialisation and 30 EC of further electives. At least 15 EC must be intermediate. External minors, courses abroad and exceptional package combinations require approval. Overlapping credit may be deducted. The example keeps the package and electives unfilled. Thesis Lab requires at least three advanced specialisation courses (22.5 EC), and students choose a linguistics or literature group appropriate to their specialisation. The lab assesses a portfolio and a proposal. Students complete the lab before the individual supervised thesis in English, which can draw on a completed level 2 or 3 course or the chosen specialisation. Two lecturers assess the thesis, with a third in case of substantial disagreement.
components: The Making of Modernity: Literature in English 1660–1850
Historical Linguistics and Language Change in the British Isles
Brave New Worlds: Literature in English 1850–1950
Old English and Early Medieval Society
Language and Identity: Researching and Writing Who We Are
Sociolinguistics of Englishes: Language Variation, Contact and Change
BA Thesis English Language and Culture
